padaccheda: इति । उक्त्वा । भगवान् । ब्रह्मा । ब्रह्मलोकजनैः । सह । बद्धपद्मासनः । अनन्तसमाधानगतः । अभवत्
anvaya: इति उक्त्वा भगवान् ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म-लोक-जनैः सह बद्ध-पद्म-आसनः (सन्) अनन्त-समाधान-गतः अभवत्
meaning_english: Having spoken thus, the Lord Brahmā, along with the inhabitants of the world of Brahman, assumed the bound lotus posture and entered a state of infinite meditative absorption.
He became established in the subtlest vibration of the Oṃkāra, his mind entirely stilled. Remaining in a form as motionless as a figure in a painting, all his perceptions reached utter quiescence.

content_sanskrit: तमेवानुसरन्ती सा तथैव ध्यानगा सती । वासनासीदशेषांशा शान्ता चाकाशरूपिणी
padaccheda: तम् । एव । अनुसरन्ती । सा । तथा । एव । ध्यानगा । सती । वासना । आसीत् । अशेषांशा । शान्ता । च । आकाशरूपिणी
anvaya: तम् एव अनुसरन्ती सा (चूडाला) तथा एव ध्यान-गा सती अशेषांशा शान्ता आकाश-रूपिणी वासना आसीत्
meaning_english: Following his example, she (Cūḍālā) likewise entered deep meditation. Becoming a residue of pure tendency, free from all parts and peaceful, she assumed the nature of the infinite space.

padaccheda: परमेष्ठिनि । असंकल्पे । तस्मिन् । तानवम् । एयुषि । सर्वगानन्तचिद्व्योमरूपः । अपश्यम् । अहम् । यदा
anvaya: तस्मिन् परमेष्ठिनि असंकल्पे तानवम् इयुषि (सति) यदा अहम् सर्व-ग-अनन्त-चित्-व्योम-रूपः अपश्यम्
meaning_english: When that Supreme Creator (Parameṣṭhin) became free from volition and attained extreme subtlety, I then beheld him in the form of the all-pervading, infinite space of consciousness.

content_sanskrit: यावत्संकल्पनं तस्य विरसीभवति क्षणात् । तथैवाशु तथैवोर्व्याः साद्रिद्वीपपयोनिधेः
padaccheda: यावत् । संकल्पनं । तस्य । विरसीभवति । क्षणात् । तथा । एव । आशु । तथा । एव । उर्व्याः । साद्रिद्वीपपयोनिधेः
anvaya: तस्य संकल्पनं यावत् क्षणात् विरसीभवति तथा एव आशु तथा एव उर्व्याः स-अद्रि-द्वीप-पयोनिधेः
meaning_english: As his creative volition faded in an instant, so too did the vitality of the earth, including its mountains, islands, and oceans, begin to wither away immediately.

padaccheda: तृणगुल्मलताशालिसमुद्भवनशक्तता । समस्ता । एव । अस्तम् । आगन्तुम् । आरब्धा । च । शनैःशनैः
anvaya: तृण-गुल्म-लता-शालि-समुद्भवन-शक्तता समस्ता एव शनैः-शनैः अस्तम् आगन्तुम् आरब्धा च
meaning_english: The power to produce grass, shrubs, creepers, and grain began to gradually vanish entirely from the world.

content_sanskrit: किल तस्य विराडात्मरूपस्याङ्गैकदेशताम् । सा बिभर्ति मही तेन तदसंवेदनोदयात्
padaccheda: किल । तस्य । विराडात्मरूपस्य । अङ्गैकदेशताम् । सा । बिभर्ति । मही । तेन । तदसंवेदनोदयात्
anvaya: सा मही तस्य विराट्-आत्म-रूपस्य अङ्ग-एक-देशताम् बिभर्ति किल तेन तत्-असंवेदन-उदयात्
meaning_english: Since the earth is indeed but a part of the limbs of that cosmic form of Virāṭ, it began to fade due to the rise of his state of non-perception.

content_sanskrit: विचेतना सा विरसा बभूव परिजर्जरा । मार्गशीर्षान्तवल्लीव जराविधुरतां गता
padaccheda: विचेतना । सा । विरसा । बभूव । परिजर्जरा । मार्गशीर्षान्तवल्ली । इव । जराविधुरताम् । गता
anvaya: सा विचेतना विरसा परिजर्जरा मार्गशीर्ष-अन्त-वल्ली इव जरा-विधुरताम् गता बभूव
meaning_english: Becoming lifeless, sapless, and completely decayed, the earth reached a state of distress and fragility, like a creeper at the end of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.

content_sanskrit: यथास्माकमसंवित्तेरङ्गाली विरसा भवेत् । तथा विरिंचिसंवित्तैर्धरा वैधुर्यमागता
padaccheda: यथा । अस्माकम् । अசंवित्तेः । अङ्गाली । विरसा । भवेत् । तथा । विरिंचिसंवित्तेः । धरा । वैधुर्यम् । आगता
anvaya: यथा अस्माकम् असंवित्तेः अङ्ग-आली विरसा भवेत् तथा विरिंचि-संवित्तैः धरा वैधुर्यम् आगता
meaning_english: Just as our own limbs lose their vigor when consciousness is withdrawn, so too did the earth fall into a state of desolation due to the withdrawal of Brahmā's consciousness.
The earth became filled and covered with the weight of numerous great calamities, while humanity, scorched by the embers of their own misdeeds, turned toward hellish suffering.
The earth became wretched due to famine, sudden calamities, misery, and poverty. It was filled with ill-behaved women and populated by lawless men.
The sun appeared grey, obscured by dust, dimness, and mist. The world was agitated by contentious people, fools, the deeply miserable, the addicted, and the diseased.
The territories were devastated by conflagrations, floods, and wars. Common people suffered and perished due to drought, lack of rain, and the ensuing hardships.
Mountains and cities collapsed under unexpected and great calamities. People wailed over the loss of children, learned Vedic scholars, sages, noblemen, and the virtuous.
Deep pits appeared unexpectedly in the middle of the ground. The people and the kings became obsessed with women born of the intermingling of castes.
All people were pained by high costs of food, crossroads were haunted by misery, women cared only for their hair, and leaders became a source of torment to the worthy.
Behaviors were pierced by sorrow, all subjects were tormented by dualities and conflict, women were afflicted by unrighteousness, and rulers were consumed by the vice of drinking.
Enveloped by the sting of unrighteousness and pierced by hundreds of false scriptures, the wicked possessed all the wealth while the virtuous were struck down by calamities.
The earth was ruled by ignoble kings who disregarded the wise. It was immersed in the dust of greed, delusion, fear, hatred, passion, and disease.
Men pursued the wives of others, noble Brāhmaṇas were assaulted by anger, and commoners at the margins were constantly engaged in loud cries of distress.

The earth has become a place where cities, villages, and the sanctuaries of gods and Brāhmaṇas are ravaged by bandits. It is fragile and treacherous at its core, appearing sweet only at the first onset of destruction while yielding nothing but sorrow.

Characterized by the misery of failed actions resulting from the indulgence in sloth, the earth reaches its end in the agony of all-encompassing calamities, with its quarters gradually becoming desolate and ruined.
With cities and villages reduced to mere ash and entire regions depopulated, the sky becomes terrifying, filled with swirling wreaths of ash-clouds that seem to wail aloud.
The earth’s interior resounds with the loud wailing of unfortunate and chaotic events; its population is reduced to a mere handful, trailing behind them the constant heat of human suffering.

content_sanskrit: नीरसाशेषदेशान्ता सर्वर्तुगुणवर्जिता । इत्यस्य पार्थिवे धातौ ब्रह्मणो गतवेदने
padaccheda: नीरसाशेषदेशान्ता । सर्वर्तुगुणवर्जिता । इति । अस्य । पार्थिवे । धातौ । ब्रह्मणः । गतवेदने
anvaya: (सा) नीरस-अशेष-देश-अन्ता सर्व-ऋतु-गुण-वर्जिता इति अस्य ब्रह्मणः पार्थिवे धातौ गत-वेदने (सति) ।
meaning_english: When this earthly element of Brahman became devoid of sensation, all regions became sapless and parched, completely stripped of the natural characteristics and virtues of the seasons.

content_sanskrit: पृथिवी पृथुवैधुर्या संपन्नासन्ननाशतः । अथ तत्संविदुन्मुक्तो जलधातुः क्षयोन्मुखः
padaccheda: पृथिवी । पृथुवैधुर्या । संपन्ना । आसन्ननाशतः । अथ । तत्संविदुन्मुक्तः । जलधातुः । क्षयोन्मुखः
anvaya: आसन्न-नाशतः पृथिवी पृथु-वैधुर्या संपन्ना अथ तत्-संवित्-उन्मुक्तः जल-धातुः क्षय-उन्मुखः (जातः) ।
meaning_english: Due to its imminent destruction, the earth fell into great desolation. Subsequently, the element of water, released from its sustaining consciousness, also moved toward dissolution.

padaccheda: यदा । विक्षुभितात्मा । आसीत् । तदा । नियत्तिलङ्घनात् । समुत्सार्य । आर्यमर्यादाम् । अर्णवाः । विवृतार्णसः
anvaya: यदा (जल-धातुः) विक्षुभित-आत्मा आसीत् तदा नियति-लङ्घनात् आर्य-मर्यादाम् समुत्सार्य अर्णवाः विवृत-अर्णसः (जाताः) ।
meaning_english: When the watery element became agitated, the oceans overstepped the bounds of cosmic order and discarded all noble limits, laying bare their vast waters in a chaotic upheaval.

content_sanskrit: प्रवृत्ता विकृतिं गन्तुमुन्मत्ता इव राविणः । वीचिविक्षोभविन्यासैर्वेलाविपिनलावकाः
padaccheda: प्रवृत्ताः । विकृतिम् । गन्तुम् । उन्मत्ताः । इव । राविणः । वीचिविक्षोभविन्यासैः । वेलाविपिनलावकाः
anvaya: उन्मत्ताः राविणः इव विकृतिं गन्तुम् प्रवृत्ताः (ते अर्णवाः) वीचि-विक्षोभ-विन्यासैः वेला-विपिन-लावकाः (जाताः) ।
meaning_english: Like roaring madmen, the oceans began to undergo a hideous transformation, their tossing waves acting as reapers that mowed down the forests along the shores.

The oceans uprooted their very foundations through the churning and whirling of massive surges, while their towering waves, swirling like great clouds, seized the very sky and the cardinal directions.
The caves of the mountains were shaken by the thunderous 'gulugulu' sound of vast whirlpools, and the mountains themselves were enveloped by the dense, massive onset of floods of spray.
The ocean interiors swirled with vigorously moving, powerful crocodiles, while their depths appeared like forests due to the trees swept away and seized by the leaping sea monsters.
Lions, falling from shattering mountain caves, struck the aquatic creatures below, while the sky became star-studded by the mass of great gems tossed upward by the surging waves.
The vast clouds in the sky were concealed by leaping crocodiles, and the atmosphere was filled with the harsh, clanging sounds of roaring echoes from the collision of opposing waves.
The sun appeared washed by the spray from the trumpeting of swimming, agitated elephants, and the mountain walls were split asunder by the violent tossing and mutual friction of the waters.
The waves, like a multitude of hands, plundered the coastal mountains, and the frenzied waters entered the thundering mountain caves as if they were their own dwellings.

content_sanskrit: भूपाः परपुराक्रान्ता लग्ना इव हतारयः । तारारवरणद्गेहविद्रावितनभश्चराः
padaccheda: भूपाः । परपुराक्रान्ताः । लग्नाः । इव । हतारयः । तारारवरणद्गेहविद्रावितनभश्चराः
anvaya: पर-पुर-आक्रान्ताः हत-अरयः लग्नाः भूपाः इव (ते) तारा-रव-रणद्-गेह-विद्रावित-नभश्चराः (बभूवुः)
meaning_english: Like kings who have conquered enemy cities and slain their foes, the waters drove away the celestial beings with the loud, ringing sounds echoing through the mountain-cavern houses.
The sky was filled with uprooted forests and looked like a woodland, while waves resembling winged mountains rose up to occupy the entire firmament.
Propelled by mountain-like billows torn by howling winds, the waters roared as they crashed against the crumbling banks of the trembling coastal mountain ranges.
Vast, surging whirlpools tossed up swarms of crocodiles, while deep, sinking eddies appeared to swallow the very mountain caves into their bottomless depths.
The waters appeared jagged with tooth-like rocks obtained from shattered caves, and sea-elephants remained submerged in the wave-filled caverns hanging from the mountain peaks.
The oceans surged, with tortoises snagged in the branches of trees overtaken by the tossing waves, as the mounts of Yama and Indra stood with ears pricked, overwhelmed by fear.
The crashing sounds of falling mountain cliffs echoed as the mountains themselves, sliced by the powerful lashings of fish tails, rapidly submerged and re-emerged.
The waters, cool with showers after effortlessly uprooting forest groves, met with the rows of flames from the blazing underwater vaḍavā fire.

anvaya: सरसेन विभोः नाशैः विशङ्कित-महा-अनलाः मिलत्-शिखरि-माला-अग्र-जल-मातङ्ग-योधिनः (ते समुद्राः) ।
meaning_english: The Great Fire feared its own destruction by the fluid mass, while the water-elephants at the crests of colliding mountain ranges engaged in fierce combat.

anvaya: जल-आवलन-वेधिनः तरङ्ग-ओघैः नृत्यन्ति इव (ते समुद्राः) जल-अचल-अचल-अन्योन्य-संघट्ट-स्फोट-पण्डिताः (अभवन्) ।
meaning_english: Agitated by the swirling waters, the oceans seemed to dance with their surging waves, becoming experts in the explosive sounds of colliding aquatic mountains.
Adorned with great mountains, forests, and multitudes of living beings, the oceans became resonant like the beating of kettle-drums by the majestic elephants of the forest.

padaccheda: असुरैः । इव । पातालं । कल्लोलैः । अलम् । आकुलाः । अथ । उदपतत् । उन्नासदिङ्नागवदनध्वनिः
anvaya: असुरैः इव कल्लोलैः पातालं अलम् आकुलाः (ते समुद्राः) अथ उत्-नास-दिङ्-नाग-वदन-ध्वनिः उदपतत् ।
meaning_english: The oceans agitated the netherworld (Pātāla) with waves like demons; then, a roar erupted from the upturned trunks of the elephants guarding the quarters.
The earth, with its mountain-pivots trembling, shook for a moment, driven by the fierce explosive pressure within the depths of the palate of Pātāla.

padaccheda: लोला । शैवालवल्ली । इव । व्यालोलाम्भोधिलङ्घिता । अथ । दुर्वारनिर्घोषनिर्वाताडम्बरान्विता
anvaya: व्यालोल-अम्भोध-लङ्घिता (सा उर्वी) लोला शैवाल-वल्ली इव (आसीत्) अथ दुर्वार-निर्घोष-निर्वात-आडम्बर-अन्विता (बभूव) ।
meaning_english: Overrun by the surging oceans, the earth appeared like a swaying moss-creeper, accompanied by the unstoppable roar and the spectacle of a windless void.

content_sanskrit: पुस्फोटेव पतन्ती द्यौर्दिशां पतिरवारवैः । आवर्तवलनाकाराः केतवः पेतुरम्बरात्
padaccheda: पुस्फोट । इव । पतन्ती । द्यौः । दिशां । पतिरवारवैः । आवर्तवलनाकाराः । केतवः । पेतुः । अम्बरात्
anvaya: पतन्ती द्यौः इव दिशां पति-रवा-रवैः पुस्फोट (तथा) अम्बरात् आवर्त-वलन-आकाराः केतवः पेतुः ।
meaning_english: The sky seemed to burst with the thunderous cries of the lords of the directions, and comets shaped like swirling whirlpools fell from the heavens.

content_sanskrit: हेमरत्नमया मुक्ताः सिन्दूरभुजगा इव । ककुब्भ्यो नभसो भूमेरुदगुर्दग्धदिक्तटाः
padaccheda: हेमरत्नमयाः । मुक्ताः । सिन्दूरभुजगाः । इव । ककुब्भ्यः । नभसः । भूमेः । उदगुः । दग्धदिक्तटाः
anvaya: (ये) हेम-रत्न-मयाः (आसन् ते) मुक्ताः सिन्दूर-भुजगाः इव दग्ध-दिक्-तटाः (सन्तः) ककुब्भ्यः नभसः भूमेः (च) उदगुः
meaning_english: Gold and jewel-encrusted objects, freed and resembling vermilion-colored serpents, rose from the directions, the sky, and the earth, while the edges of the quarters appeared scorched.

padaccheda: चलज्ज्वालाजटाटोपाः । विविधोत्पातपङ्कयः । पृथ्व्यादीनि । असुरादीनि । ब्रह्मोन्मुक्तानि । सर्वतः
anvaya: चलत्-ज्वाला-जटा-टोपाः विविध-उत्पात-पङ्क्तयः (च) पृथ्व्यादीनि असुरादीनि ब्रह्म-उन्मुक्तानि सर्वतः (आसन्)
meaning_english: Clusters of various portents with the terrifying appearance of moving massed flames emerged, as the elements starting with earth and beings starting with the Asuras were released by Brahma from all sides.

padaccheda: द्विविधानि । महाभूतानि । अलम् । संक्षोभम् । आययुः । चन्द्रार्कानिलशक्राग्नियमाः । कोलाहलाकुलाः
anvaya: द्विविधानि महाभूतानि अलम् संक्षोभम् आययुः चन्द्र-अर्क-अनिल-शक्र-अग्नि-यमाः कोलाहल-आकुलाः (आसन्)
meaning_english: The two-fold great elements underwent extreme agitation, while Candra, Arka, Anila, Śakra, Agni, and Yama became overwhelmed by the tumultuous chaos.
The lords residing in Brahmaloka were intent on falling, as rows of trees collapsed with cracking sounds due to the violent tremors.

padaccheda: भूमेः । अन्वभवन् । भूरिदोलान्दोलनम् । अद्रयः । भूकम्पलोलकैलासमेरुमन्दरकन्दराः । पेतुः । कल्पतरून्मुक्ताः । रक्तस्तबकवृष्टयः
anvaya: अद्रयः भूमेः भूरि-दोला-आन्दोलनम् अन्वभवन् भू-कम्प-लोल-कैलास-मेरु-मन्दर-कन्दराः (आसन्) कल्प-तरु-उन्मुक्ताः रक्त-स्तबक-वृष्टयः पेतुः
meaning_english: The mountains experienced heavy swinging oscillations of the earth; the caves of Kailāsa, Meru, and Mandara shook from earthquakes, and rains of red flower-clusters released from the Kalpataru trees fell down.

content_sanskrit: लोकान्तराद्रिपुरवारिधिकाननान्तमुत्पातकल्पपवनेन मिथो हतानाम् । कोलाहलैर्जगदभूत्प्रविकीर्णशीर्णं पूर्णार्णवे त्रिपुरपूर इवाभिपाती
padaccheda: लोकान्तराद्रिपुरवारिधिकाननान्तम् । उत्पातकल्पपवनेन । मिथः । हतानाम् । कोलाहलैः । जगत् । अभूत् । प्रविकीर्णशीर्णं । पूर्णार्णवे । त्रिपुरपूरः । इव । अभिपाती
anvaya: लोक-अन्तर-अद्रि-पुर-वारिधि-कानन-अन्तम् उत्पात-कल्प-पवनेन मिथः हतानाम् कोलाहलैः जगत् पूर्ण-अर्णवे अभिपाती त्रिपुर-पुरः इव प्रविकीर्ण-शीर्णम् अभूत्
meaning_english: Due to the clamor of mountains, cities, oceans, and forests from other worlds striking one another by the gale of the cataclysmic portents, the world became scattered and shattered, like the city of Tripura falling into the full ocean.
